sections.title: Performance Analysis
sections.content:
Note on scope: the pasted "Codebase Context" is almost entirely test files and pure presentation/formatting utilities (`format.ts`, `ranking.ts`, `decisions-shared.ts`, `incident-format.ts`, the `ink/` component tests) — none of that layer touches a DB, does data fetching, or renders lists, so there's nothing actionable in it for this audit. I instead swept the real hot paths (`src/lib/**/*.server.ts`, `src/lib/*.functions.ts`, `src/components/discover|knowledge`) and cross-checked against items flagged in earlier same-day audits rather than re-report stale claims. Two of three previously-flagged "open" items turned out to already be fixed in the live code; one wasn't (a session note claimed a fix that isn't actually in the file — flagging that discrepancy too).

---

sections.title: 1. N+1 query / N+1 remote-call patterns
2. Unnecessary React re-renders
sections.content:
Swept `src/components/discover/{SignalFeed,OpportunityQueue,ThemeRow}.tsx` (flagged in the 2026-07-17 audit for inline-closure re-render leaks) and `src/components/knowledge/CalendarPanel.tsx` (flagged 2026-07-18/19 for unmemoized filter/sort/groupBy). All four are now genuinely fixed:

- `OpportunityQueue.tsx:39` wraps rows in `memo(function BoundOpportunityRow...)` with a comment explicitly noting handlers must be stable per mount to keep the memo effective, backed by `useCallback` for every row action (lines 82-90).
- `SignalFeed.tsx` and `ThemeRow.tsx` similarly use `useMemo`/`useCallback`/`memo`.
- `CalendarPanel.tsx:321` wraps the item aggregation (`filter`/`sort`) in a single `useMemo`.

No new re-render regressions found in this pass within budget. If you want deeper coverage, the `ink/` primitives (`Card`, `Input`, `Modal`) are stateless and low-risk; the highest-value next targets for a re-render sweep would be the canvas-heavy files (`GraphUniverseCanvas.tsx`, `GraphForceCanvas.tsx`, `GraphCanvasView.tsx`) since they mix imperative canvas drawing with React state — worth a dedicated pass if you want it.

---

sections.title: 3. Caching opportunities
sections.content:
- `src/router.tsx:122` sets a sane global React Query `staleTime: 30_000` — confirmed all settings components (`TeamCard`, `ProductsTab`, `DataExportCard`, `IntegrationsTab`) consume the shared client via `useQueryClient()` rather than instantiating their own (would have silently defeated caching) — checked, no issue.
- BYOK key resolution caching across retry/fallback attempts already shipped in `runtime.server.ts` (commit `c553d4c0`).
- New opportunity: **eval-runner.server.ts** resolves the suite/prompt row once before the loop (good — not redundant), but if `runEvalSuite` is invoked repeatedly by the scheduled tick (per the file's own doc comment: "invoked from a serverFn or from the scheduled eval-suite-tick hook"), there's no suite-level result caching between ticks — likely fine given eval suites are meant to re-run, just noting it's not a cache gap so much as intended behavior.

---

sections.title: 4. Memory leaks
sections.content:
Swept every `setInterval`/`setTimeout`/`addEventListener`/`ResizeObserver`/`IntersectionObserver`/`requestAnimationFrame` call site under `src/components/**/*.tsx` (23 files). **Every single one has a matching cleanup in the `useEffect` return** — `clearInterval`, `removeEventListener`, `.disconnect()`, `clearTimeout`, or `cancelAnimationFrame`, including the previously-flagged `GraphUniverseCanvas.tsx:586` RAF loop, which now correctly does `cancelAnimationFrame(rafId.current)`. No open leaks found. This area has clearly already had a thorough remediation pass — nothing further to flag.

---

sections.title: 5. Redundant computations
sections.content:
No new instances found beyond the already-fixed `CalendarPanel.tsx` case. `agentDisplayName()` (`src/lib/agent-vocabulary.ts:685`) — called per-row in `decisions-shared.ts:displayWho` — is a pure in-memory catalog lookup, not a hidden expensive call, so no issue despite being invoked per row.

---

sections.title: Summary / priority order
sections.content:
| # | File | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `eval-runner.server.ts:148-236` | Serial AI calls, no concurrency (buffer note claiming a fix was wrong) | **Open — do first** |
| 2 | `meetings.functions.ts:192-199` | N+1 `stage_events` insert per decision | **Open — trivial fix** |
| 3 | `assumption-watch.server.ts:136-152` | N+1 serial judge calls + per-row update | **Open — safe to parallelize** |
| 4 | `supersession.server.ts:110-140` | Per-edge sequential upsert | Open, lower priority |
| 5 | Re-renders (discover/*, CalendarPanel) | — | Already fixed, verified |
| 6 | Memory leaks (23 files swept) | — | Already fixed, verified |
| 7 | `lineage.functions.ts`, `linear.functions.ts` | N+1 writes | Already fixed, verified |

Want me to implement fixes 1-3 now (they're small, isolated, and each has a concrete diff above), or hand this off to a background agent to do all four plus a deeper re-render pass on the canvas components?
